DAMGHANI:v1p180/r9.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p180/r9.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p180/r9.claim: Dhikr can mean revelation or revealed message.
DAMGHANI:v1p180/r9.anchor: التاسع : الذكر بمعنى الوحي قوله تعالى في سورة القمر

SAMIN-DURR:15:6/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:15:6/r1.speaker: العامة
SAMIN-DURR:15:6/r1.claim: The common reading has نزل doubled and passive.
SAMIN-DURR:15:6/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: { نزل عليه الذكر } العامة على " نزل " مشددا مبنيا للمفعول

SAMIN-DURR:15:6/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:15:6/r2.speaker: زيد بن علي
SAMIN-DURR:15:6/r2.claim: Zayd ibn Ali reads نزل lightly and actively.
SAMIN-DURR:15:6/r2.anchor: وزيد بن علي " نزل " مخففا مبنيا للفاعل.

ASAD-NOTES:15:6/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:15:6/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:15:6/r1.claim: The deniers address the Prophet as one who allegedly received the reminder from on high and call him mad.
ASAD-NOTES:15:6/r1.anchor: O thou unto whom this reminder has [allegedly] been bestowed from on high: verily, thou art mad

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Earlier messengers were mocked too; the Prophet’s nation repeats a familiar pattern and will share the predecessors’ fate.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: What he is experiencing today from his nation is nothing new; previous prophets too faced a similar response from their nations.

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p182/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p182/r2.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p182/r2.claim: Even if accepted, the alleged praise would mean “according to you,” not endorse the idols; Arabic can voice a claim with an understood qualification, as in the cited sarcastic and hostile addresses.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p182/r2.anchor: ولكن يكون التقدير فيه: تلك الغرانقة الأولى. وإن شفاعتهن لترتجى عندكم

IBNHISHAM:v1p620/r1.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v1p620/r1.speaker: الحباب بن المنذر بن الجموح
IBNHISHAM:v1p620/r1.claim: Al-Ḥubāb asks whether the Prophet’s position at Badr is divinely fixed or tactical; when told it is strategy, he advises securing the nearest water, blocking wells behind it, and filling a basin. The Prophet approves and carries out the plan.
IBNHISHAM:v1p620/r1.anchor: أن الحباب بن المنذر بن الجموح قال: يا رسول الله، أرأيت هذا المنزل، أمنزلا أنزلكه الله ليس لنا أن نتقدمه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p466/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p466/r5.speaker: مقاتل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p466/r5.claim: Muqātil says verses 6–9 were revealed concerning ʿAbd Allāh b. Umayya, al-Naḍr b. al-Ḥārith, Nawfal b. Khuwaylid, and al-Walīd b. al-Mughīra.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p466/r5.anchor: قال مقاتل: نزلت في عبد الله بن أمية، والنضر بن الحرث، ونوفل بن خويلد، والوليد بن المغيرة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p466/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p466/r6.speaker: زيد بن علي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p466/r6.claim: Zayd b. ʿAlī reads nazala in the past, light form, active voice.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p466/r6.anchor: وقرأ زيد بن علي: نزل عليه الذكر ماضيا مخففا مبنيا للفاعل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p466/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p466/r7.speaker: زيد بن علي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p466/r7.claim: Zayd b. ʿAlī also reads ‘O you to whom the Reminder was cast’; the author treats this as explanatory because it differs from the written consonantal text.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p466/r7.anchor: وقرأ: يا أيها الذي ألقي إليه الذكر، وينبغي أن تجعل هذه القراءة تفسيرا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p466/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p466/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p466/r8.claim: The address ‘the one on whom the Reminder was sent down’ is sarcastic: they do not accept its revelation and accuse the Prophet of madness.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p466/r8.anchor: وهذا الوصف بأنه الذي نزل عليه الذكر قالوه على جهة الاستهزاء والاستخفاف

ALUSI-FULL:v14p11#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p11#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p11#2/r1.claim: The passage begins describing the Meccans’ rejection of the one who brought the Book, their rejection of the Book, and the outcome awaiting them.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p11#2/r1.anchor: شروع في بيان كفرهم بمن أنزل عليه الكتاب المتضمن للكفر به وبيان ما يؤل إليه حالهم والقائل أهل مكة

ALUSI-FULL:v14p11#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p11#2/r2.speaker: مقاتل
ALUSI-FULL:v14p11#2/r2.claim: Muqātil says the verse was revealed about ʿAbd Allāh b. Umayya, al-Naḍr b. al-Ḥārith, Nawfal b. Khuwaylid, and al-Walīd b. al-Mughīra, who addressed the Prophet with these words.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p11#2/r2.anchor: قال مقاتل : نزلت الآية في عبدالله بن أمية والنضر ابن الحرث ونوفل بن خويلد والوليد بن المغيرة

ALUSI-FULL:v14p11#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p11#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p11#2/r3.claim: Al-dhikr refers to the Qurʾān; the disbelievers’ address is sarcastic even though they deny that any revelation descended.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p11#2/r3.anchor: أي القرآن وخاطبوه عليه الصلاة والسلام بذلك مع أنهم الكفرة الذين لا يعتقدون نزول شيء استهزاء وتهكما

ALUSI-FULL:v14p11#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p11#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p11#2/r4.claim: They imply that claiming such an extraordinary revelation proves the Prophet is certainly mad, like calling someone mad for saying something one finds incredible; this best fits the context.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p11#2/r4.anchor: يعنون يا من يدعي مثل هذا الأمر العظيم الخارق للعادة إنك بسبب تلك الدعوى متحقق جنونك

ALUSI-FULL:v14p11#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p11#2/r5.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v14p11#2/r5.claim: Another explanation is that they called him mad because he appeared faint when the Qurʾān was being revealed to him.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p11#2/r5.anchor: وقيل : حكمهم هذا لما يظهر عليه الصلاة والسلام من شبه الغشي حين ينزل عليه الوحي بالقرآن

ALUSI-FULL:v14p11#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p11#2/r6.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v14p11#2/r6.claim: Some take only the emphatic ‘you are mad’ as the disbelievers’ speech, while God supplies the address to clear the Prophet from the charge immediately; al-Ālūsī objects that this poorly fits the next verse’s rebuttal, though it could answer their implication.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p11#2/r6.anchor: ذهب بعضهم إلى أن القول الجملة المؤكدة دون النداء أما هو فمن كلام الله تعالى تبرئة له عليه الصلاة والسلام

ALUSI-FULL:v14p11#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p11#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p11#2/r7.claim: The wording recalls Pharaoh’s earlier description of Moses’ messenger as mad.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p11#2/r7.anchor: وقد سبقهم إلى نظيره فرعون عليه اللعنة بقوله في حق موسى عليه السلام

ALUSI-FULL:v14p11#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p11#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p11#2/r8.claim: Fronting ‘upon him’ reflects that their denial concerns whether the reminder descends from God, unlike 43:31, where the objection targets the chosen recipient after accepting revelation’s source.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p11#2/r8.anchor: لأن إنكارهم متوجه إلى كون النازل ذكرا من الله تعالى لا إلى كون المنزل عليه رسول الله

ALUSI-FULL:v14p12/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p12/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p12/r1.claim: The passive can imply that the claimed descent has no agent, or direct the denial toward its being revealed to the Prophet rather than toward its attribution to a sender.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p12/r1.anchor: وإيراد الفعل على صيغة المجهول لا يهام أن ذلك ليس بفعل له فاعل أو لتوجيه الإنكار إلى كون التنزيل عليه

ALUSI-FULL:v14p12/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p12/r2.speaker: زيد بن علي
ALUSI-FULL:v14p12/r2.claim: Zayd b. ʿAlī read nazzala actively and raised al-dhikr as its subject.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p12/r2.anchor: وقرأ زيد بن علي رضي الله تعالى عنهما نزل عليه الذكر بتخفيف ( نزل ) مبنيا للفاعل ورفع ( الذكر )

ALUSI-FULL:v14p12/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p12/r3.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v14p12/r3.claim: Abū Ḥayyān says the reading ‘the one upon whom the reminder was cast’ should be treated as an explanatory gloss because it differs from the muṣḥaf consonantal text.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p12/r3.anchor: قال أبو حيان : وينبغي أن تجعل هذه القراءة تفسيرا لمخالفتها سواد المصحف

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p369/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p369/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p369/r4.claim: The Meccan polytheists address Muḥammad as the one upon whom the Reminder, meaning the Qur'an, was sent.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p369/r4.anchor: {وقالوا} يعني: مشركي مكة {يا أيها الذي نزل عليه الذكر} أي: القرآن، وأرادوا به محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p369/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p369/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p369/r5.claim: They sarcastically mention the Reminder's descent while calling Muḥammad mad.

BAYDAWI-FULL:15:5-7/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:15:5-7/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:15:5-7/r3.claim: They address the Prophet with this title mockingly, then call him insane for claiming God sent down the Reminder, the Qur’an.
BAYDAWI-FULL:15:5-7/r3.anchor: نادوا به النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم على التهكم، ألا ترى إلى ما نادوه له

BAYDAWI-FULL:15:5-7/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:15:5-7/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:15:5-7/r4.claim: Their charge means that claiming God sent down the Qur’an is the speech of a madman.
BAYDAWI-FULL:15:5-7/r4.anchor: والمعنى إنك لتقول قول المجانين حين تدعي أن الله تعالى نزل عليك الذكر، أي القرآن.

BAYDAWI-FULL:15:5-7/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:15:5-7/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:15:5-7/r5.claim: The taunt echoes Pharaoh’s accusation that the messenger sent to him was mad.
BAYDAWI-FULL:15:5-7/r5.anchor: ونظير ذلك قول فرعون: إن رسولكم الذى أرسل إليكم لمجنون

BIQAI-FULL:v4p205/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p205/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p205/r7.claim: Their passive wording reflects their denial of revelation itself; they name it mockingly, as if only Muhammad claimed it was sent down.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p205/r7.anchor: ولما كان تكذيبهم بالتنزيل نفسه , بني للمفعول

BIQAI-FULL:v4p205/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p205/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p205/r8.claim: They call Muhammad mad because he claims God sent him a Reminder, alleging that a jinn confuses him; their insult substitutes for an answer to the preceding argument and exposes their stubbornness.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p205/r8.anchor: فكان هذا دليلا علة عنادهم , فإنهم أقاموا الشتم مقام الجواب

DURR-FULL:v5p66/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p66/r2.speaker: الضحاك
DURR-FULL:v5p66/r2.claim: Al-Dahhak identifies the Reminder revealed to Muhammad as the Qur’an.
DURR-FULL:v5p66/r2.anchor: عن الضحاك في قوله: {وقالوا يا أيها الذي نزل عليه الذكر} قال: القرآن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p16/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p16/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p16/r1.claim: This is conjoined to the command to leave them in 15:3: that clause depicts indulgence and hopes, while this depicts deeper disbelief and denial of Muḥammad's message.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p16/r1.anchor: والمناسبة أن المعطوف عليها تضمنت انهماكهم في الملذات والآمال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p16/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p16/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p16/r2.claim: The sense is to leave them to disbelieve and say all manner of things in denial and mockery.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p16/r2.anchor: والمعنى : ذرهم يكذبون ويقولون شتى القول من التكذيب والاستهزاء .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p16/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p16/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p16/r3.claim: The whole sentence is presented as the polytheists' own speech.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p16/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p16/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p16/r4.claim: The vocative publicly spotlights the description; the relative clause is selected because they pretend that revelation is grounds for mockery, as the insult that follows shows.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p16/r4.anchor: لما في الصلة من المعنى الذي جعلوه سبب التهكم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p16/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p16/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p16/r5.claim: The Prophet told ʿĀʾisha that God diverted the polytheists' abuse: they insulted Mudhammam while he was Muḥammad.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p16/r5.anchor: فقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لعائشة : ( ألم تري كيف صرف الله عني أذى المشركين وسبهم ، يسبون مذمما وأنا محمد )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p16/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p16/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p16/r6.claim: The relative clause attributes the description to the referent according to what those using the title claim, not according to the speaker's own belief; this is mockery.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p16/r6.anchor: وفي هذا إسناد الصلة إلى الموصول بحسب ما يدعيه صاحب اسم الموصول ، لا بحسب اعتقاد المتكلم على طريقة التهكم .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p16/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p16/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p16/r7.claim: Dhikr can mean verbal utterance or recollection; the revealed speech is called dhikr because it is recited and repeated, reminds of God and the Last Day, or gives later generations a remembrance of them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p16/r7.anchor: فالذكر الكلام الموحى به ليتلى ويكرر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p16/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p16/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p16/r8.claim: Calling the Qur'an dhikr is a remarkably comprehensive naming that Arabs had not known before its appearance in the Qur'an.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p16/r8.anchor: فتسمية القرآن ذكرا تسمية جامعة عجيبة لم يكن للعرب علم بها من قبل أن ترد في القرآن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p16/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p16/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p16/r9.claim: Qurʾān names the revelation for its intended recitation; dhikr and qurʾān name forms of discourse meant for people's reception and recitation, like poetry, sermons, stories, and fables.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p16/r9.anchor: وكذلك تسميته قرآنا لأنه قصد من إنزاله أن يقرأ ، فصار الذكر والقرآن صنفين من أصناف الكلام الذي يلقى للناس

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p351/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p351/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p351/r1.claim: The speakers are Quraysh unbelievers; a report names ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Umayya, al-Naḍr ibn al-Ḥārith, and others like them.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p351/r1.anchor: الضمير في قالوا يراد به كفار قريش. ويروى أن القائلين كانوا: عبد الله بن أبي أمية، والنضر بن الحارث

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p351/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p351/r2.speaker: الأعمش
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p351/r2.claim: Al-Aʿmash reads ‘O you to whom the Reminder was cast down’ in place of ‘was sent down.’
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p351/r2.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش: «يا أيها الذي ألقي إليه الذكر» .

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p351/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p351/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p351/r3.claim: Their address is derisive, meaning ‘according to your claim’; he compares it to sarcastically calling an ignorant man a scholar who cannot even perform ablution.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p351/r3.anchor: وقولهم: يا أيها الذي نزل عليه الذكر كلام على جهة الاستخفاف، أي بزعمك ودعواك، وهذه المخاطبة كما تقول لرجل جاهل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p383#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p383#2/r1.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p383#2/r1.claim: Muqatil says the verse was revealed about Abdullah ibn Abi Umayya, al-Nadr ibn al-Harith, Nawfal ibn Khuwaylid, and al-Walid ibn al-Mughira.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p383#2/r1.anchor: قال مقاتل نزلت في عبد الله بن أبي أمية والنضر بن الحارث ونوفل بن خويلد والوليد بن المغيرة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p383#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p383#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p383#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says al-dhikr refers to the Quran; the accusation that its recipient was mad was mockery, since belief in the revelation would have prevented such a taunt.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p383#2/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس والذكر القرآن وإنما قالوا هذا استهزاء لو أيقنوا أنه نزل عليه الذكر ما قالوا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p383#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p383#2/r3.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p383#2/r3.claim: Abu Ali al-Farisi points to the answer in al-Qalam 2: ‘By your Lord's blessing, you are not mad.’
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p383#2/r3.anchor: قال أبو علي الفارس وجواب هه الآية في سورة أخرى في قوله ﴿ ما أنت بنعمة ربك بمجنون ﴾ القلم 2

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p527/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p527/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p527/r1.claim: The disbelievers taunt the Prophet as one who merely claims revelation and call him mad for inviting them to follow him and abandon their inherited religion.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p527/r1.anchor: أي: الذي يدعي ذلك {إنك لمجنون} أي: في دعائك إيانا إلى اتباعك وترك ما وجدنا عليه آباءنا

JISHUMI:v6p3923/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p3923/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p3923/r11.claim: They answer the warning with mockery, calling the Prophet mad.
JISHUMI:v6p3923/r11.anchor: ما ذكر من الوعيد لهم قابلوه استهزاء ورموه بالجنون.

MUQATIL:15:4-7/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:15:4-7/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:15:4-7/r3.claim: Muqatil says the insult was revealed concerning Quraysh men Abdullah ibn Umayya ibn al-Mughira, al-Nadr ibn al-Harith, Nawfal ibn Khuwaylid, and al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, who called the Prophet mad; dhikr means Quran.
MUQATIL:15:4-7/r3.anchor: نزلت في عبد الله بن أمية بن المغيرة المخزومي

NASAFI-FULL:v2p237#5/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p237#5/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p237#5/r1.claim: The speakers are the unbelievers; al-dhikr means the Qurʾān, and they address Muḥammad as one to whom it was sent down.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p237#5/r1.anchor: ﴿ وقالوا ﴾ أي الكفار ﴿ يا أيها الذي نزل عليه الذكر ﴾ أي القرآن

NASAFI-FULL:v2p237#5/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p237#5/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p237#5/r2.claim: The taunt is mockery: they acknowledge the Qurʾān's descent while calling Muḥammad mad, deliberately reversing their words to ridicule him and saying he speaks like a madman when he claims revelation.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p237#5/r2.anchor: وكيف يقرون بنزول الذكر عليه وينسبونه إلى الجنون والتعكيس في كلامهم للاستهزاء والتهكم سائغ

NASAFI-FULL:v2p237#5/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p237#5/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p237#5/r3.claim: The commentary compares this taunt with Pharaoh's charge of madness and with other sarcastic Qurʾānic expressions.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p237#5/r3.anchor: كما قال فرعون ان رسولكم الذي ارسل اليكم لمجنون وكيف يقرون بنزول الذكر

QURTUBI-FULL:15:6-7/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:15:6-7/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:15:6-7/r1.claim: Quraysh addressed Muhammad mockingly as mad, then asked him to bring angels as proof of his truthfulness.
QURTUBI-FULL:15:6-7/r1.anchor: قاله كفار قريش لمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم على جهة الاستهزاء، ثم طلبوا منه إتيان الملائكة

RAZI-FULL:v19p125#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p125#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p125#2/r1.claim: After emphasizing threats to the unbelievers, God presents their objections to the Prophet's claim.
RAZI-FULL:v19p125#2/r1.anchor: اعلم أنه تعالى لما بالغ في تهديد الكفار ذكر بعده شبههم في إنكار نبوته

RAZI-FULL:v19p125#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p125#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p125#2/r2.claim: One explanation is that revelation brought on a faint-like state, which they mistook for madness; other verses deny that he was mad.
RAZI-FULL:v19p125#2/r2.anchor: الأول : أنه عليه السلام كان يظهر عليه عند نزول الوحي حالة شبيهة بالغشي

RAZI-FULL:v19p125#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p125#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p125#2/r3.claim: Alternatively, they thought his being a true messenger from God implausible and called him mad because his teaching seemed beyond reason.
RAZI-FULL:v19p125#2/r3.anchor: والثاني : أنم كانوا يستبعدون كونه رسولا حقا من عند الله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v19p125#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p125#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p125#2/r4.claim: They may have used the address sarcastically, as Pharaoh insulted Moses and Shuʿayb's people used praise ironically; the Qur'an also uses glad tidings ironically for punishment.
RAZI-FULL:v19p125#2/r4.anchor: الأول : أنهم ذكروه على سبيل الاستهزاء كما قال فرعون : { إن رسولكم الذى أرسل إليكم

RAZI-FULL:v19p125#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p125#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p125#2/r5.claim: Alternatively, the description means the one upon whom Reminder was sent according to his own claim and the belief of his companions and followers.
RAZI-FULL:v19p125#2/r5.anchor: الثاني : { وقالوا يأيها الذى نزل عليه الذكر } في زعمه واعتقاده ، وعند أصحابه وأتباعه

STUDYQURAN:15:6/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:15:6/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:15:6/r1.claim: The Reminder here refers to the Quran.
STUDYQURAN:15:6/r1.anchor: The Reminder here refers to the Quran

STUDYQURAN:15:6/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:15:6/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:15:6/r2.claim: Elsewhere in the Quran, Reminder can refer to scriptures revealed before the Quran.
STUDYQURAN:15:6/r2.anchor: elsewhere in the Quran the Reminder can also refer to the scriptures preceding the Quran

STUDYQURAN:15:6/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:15:6/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:15:6/r3.claim: A report says the Makkan idolaters heard the Prophet say God had sent down the Reminder to him, prompting their wording in this verse.
STUDYQURAN:15:6/r3.anchor: It is reported that the Makkan idolaters heard the Prophet say, “Verily God (Most High) has sent down the Reminder unto me”

STUDYQURAN:15:6/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:15:6/r4.speaker: al-Ṭabrisī
STUDYQURAN:15:6/r4.claim: Al-Ṭabrisī says the opponents' wording mocked the Prophet rather than affirming their belief in him as God's Messenger.
STUDYQURAN:15:6/r4.anchor: as al-Ṭabrisī notes, it was a way of mocking him

STUDYQURAN:15:6/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:15:6/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:15:6/r5.claim: The charge of possession was also leveled at other prophets, including Moses and Noah, as well as the Prophet Muhammad.
STUDYQURAN:15:6/r5.anchor: this charge of being possessed is also leveled against the other prophets

TABATABAI:15:9/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:9/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:9/r1.claim: The sūra addresses unbelievers' mockery of the Prophet as mad and their dismissal of the Qur'an as lunatic rambling; it consoles him, commands patience and forbearance, and warns and gives glad tidings.
TABATABAI:15:9/r1.anchor: بيان تشتمل السورة على الكلام حول استهزاء الكفار بالنبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

TABATABAI:15:1-9#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:1-9#2/r1.claim: The taunt is framed as mockery: they address Muhammad by the alleged revelation rather than his name, use a passive verb to distance themselves from its claimed source, and call him mad to deny him.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#2/r1.anchor: كلام خارج مخرج الاستهزاء، ولذلك خاطبوه صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم لا باسمه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p542/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p542/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p542/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: {وقالوا يا أيها الذي نزل عليه الذكر} أي: القرآن

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p542/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p542/r2.speaker: ابن عباس عن عطاء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p542/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas, in Ata's transmission, says the address is mockery: if they believed the reminder had been sent down to him, they would not call him mad.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p542/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس في رواية عطاء: هذا استهزاء منهم لو أيقنوا أنه نزل عليه الذكر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p542/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p542/r3.speaker: أبو علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p542/r3.claim: Abu Ali says the mockers do not believe revelation came to the Prophet; they mean one upon whom the reminder was sent in his own view or his followers' view, like taunts calling someone mighty or a magician.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p542/r3.anchor: وذكر أبو علي وجها آخر هو لأصحاب المعاني فقال: الذين يقولون للنبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - مجنون لا يقرون بإنزال الذكر عليه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p542/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p542/r4.speaker: زهرة اليمن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p542/r4.claim: The poet Zahra al-Yaman boasts that he is the splendid one and the flower of Yemen; the example shows an epithet can be spoken as the addressee's own claim.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p542/r4.anchor: وقد قال زهرة اليمن (¬2): أبلغ كليبا وأبلغ عنك شاعرها ... أني الأغر وأني زهرة اليمن (¬3)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p542/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p542/r5.speaker: جرير
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p542/r5.claim: Jarir answers Zahra al-Yaman, asking whether advice is already apparent in his identifying marks; this reinforces that the boastful epithet is in the speaker's own estimation.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p542/r5.anchor: (وأجابه جرير: ألم يكن في وسوم قد وسمت بها ... من حان موعظة يازهرة اليمن) (¬4)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p544/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p544/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p544/r1.claim: Majnun derives from the root for covering: forms of the verb mean becoming or being made mad, and dense intertwined plants are called majnun because parts cover one another.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p544/r1.anchor: يقال: جن فلان فهو مجنون، وقد أجنه الله، وبه جنون وجنة ومجنة، وأصله من الستر

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:15:5-12/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:15:5-12/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:15:5-12/r2.claim: The Reminder is the Qur'an, and the address was mocking.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:15:5-12/r2.anchor: { وقالوا يا أيها الذي نزل عليه الذكر } أي: القرآن. قالوا هذا استهزاء.

ELMALILI:15:6-7/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:15:6-7/r1.speaker: Mukātil
ELMALILI:15:6-7/r1.claim: Mukātil identifies Abdullah b. Umayya, Nadr b. Harith, Nawfal b. Khuwaylid, and Walid b. Mughira as the occasion for the revelation.
ELMALILI:15:6-7/r1.anchor: Mukātil‘in beyânına göre sebeb-i nüzûlü; Abdullah b. Ümeyye, Nadr b. Hâris, Nevfel b. Huveylid, Velid b. Mugīre’dir

ELMALILI:15:6-7/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:15:6-7/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:15:6-7/r2.claim: Al-Dhikr here is the Qur'an, so called because it reminds people of God's admonitions and exhortations.
ELMALILI:15:6-7/r2.anchor: “o zikir” Kur’an’dır. Çünkü Kur’an Hak teâlâ’nın halka va‘z u nasihatlerini tezkir ettiği cihetle bir ismi de “ez-Zikr”dir

ELMALILI:15:6-7/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:15:6-7/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:15:6-7/r3.claim: The polytheists use the description of one receiving the Reminder mockingly, not as an expression of belief or acceptance, to introduce their charge of madness.
ELMALILI:15:6-7/r3.anchor: teslim ve itikad suretiyle değil, ber vech-i âtî cünun hezeyanlarının illeti olmak üzere istihzâ tavrıyla yapıyorlardı

ELMALILI:15:6-7/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:15:6-7/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:15:6-7/r4.claim: As Pharaoh called Moses mad (26:27), these opponents rejected the warnings and Muhammad's prophethood as irrational, citing his absorbed state during revelation as supposed evidence.
ELMALILI:15:6-7/r4.anchor: dediği gibi bunlar da Kur’ân’ın inzarları hoşlarına gitmediği için vahy-i Kur’ân’ı

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:15:6/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:15:6/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:15:6/r1.claim: Dhikr has dictionary senses including memorizing, remembering, mentioning, and praising; the commentary renders it here as revelation.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:15:6/r1.anchor: “Vahiy”diye çevirdiğimiz zikir kelimesi sözlükte “ezberleme, hatırlama, anma, övme”gibi anlamlara gelir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:15:6/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:15:6/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:15:6/r2.claim: In the Qur'an, dhikr can mean God's warning, admonition, or revelation, earlier scriptures, and the Qur'an itself, as in verses 6 and 9 here.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:15:6/r2.anchor: Kur’an-ı Kerîm’de ise –bu sözlük anlamları yanında– özellikle “Allah’ın kullarına gönderdiği uyarı, öğüt, vahiy” vb. mânalarda geçtiği gibi daha önceki bazı kutsal kitaplar

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:15:6/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:15:6/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:15:6/r3.claim: Hadiths identify dhikr as one of the Qur'an's names; the commentary cites Tirmidhi, Book of the Merits of the Qur'an, report 14.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:15:6/r3.anchor: Nitekim hadislerde Kur’an’ın bir isminin de “zikir” olduğu bildirilir (meselâ bk. Tirmizî, “Sevâbü’l-Kur’ân”, 14)

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:15:6/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:15:6/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:15:6/r4.claim: The polytheists addressed Muhammad as one receiving revelation to mock him, not because they believed revelation had come to him.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:15:6/r4.anchor: Müşrikler Hz. Peygamber’e, “Ey kendisine vahiy gelen adam!” diye hitap ederken ona vahiy geldiğine inandıkları için böyle konuşmuyor, aksine onunla alay ediyorlardı

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:15:6/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:15:6/r5.speaker: müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:15:6/r5.claim: Commentators say the polytheists may have used the charge of madness metaphorically as mockery.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:15:6/r5.anchor: Müfessirlerin görüşüne göre müşrikler Hz. Peygamber’i mecnun diye itham ederken bunu ya alay maksadıyla mecaz anlamında

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:15:6/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:15:6/r6.speaker: müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:15:6/r6.claim: Commentators also allow that the polytheists may have meant the accusation of madness literally.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:15:6/r6.anchor: Müfessirlerin görüşüne göre müşrikler Hz. Peygamber’i mecnun diye itham ederken bunu ya alay maksadıyla mecaz anlamında veya hakikat anlamında söylüyorlardı

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:15:6/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:15:6/r7.speaker: Râzî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:15:6/r7.claim: Razi suggests that the unusual, near-trance state Muhammad displayed during revelation may have been mistaken for possession by a jinn and so called madness.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:15:6/r7.anchor: Râzî’ye göre (XIX, 158) bu suçlamanın iki sebebi olabilir: ☼a) Vahyin gelişi sırasında Hz. Peygamber’de genellikle kendinden geçmişçesine olağan üstü bir hal görülürdü

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:15:6/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:15:6/r8.speaker: Râzî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:15:6/r8.claim: Razi also suggests that they regarded Muhammad's claim to be a genuine divinely commissioned messenger as intellectually impossible, like the ravings of a madman.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:15:6/r8.anchor: Râzî’ye göre (XIX, 158) bu suçlamanın iki sebebi olabilir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:15:6/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:15:6/r9.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:15:6/r9.claim: Pre-Islamic Arab pagans believed poets received jinn-inspired poetry; Muhammad's contemporaries therefore thought the Qur'an, which they treated as poetry, came from jinn rather than God.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:15:6/r9.anchor: Eskiden Arap putperestleri şairlerin cinlerle ilişkisi bulunduğuna, şiirin de böyle bir bağlantının sonucu olarak şairlerin cinlerden aldıkları ilhamın ürünü olduğuna inanırlardı

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:15:6/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:15:6/r10.speaker: Ateş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:15:6/r10.claim: Ateş suggests that mecnun may mean someone connected with jinn, rather than simply a madman, in the polytheists' usage.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:15:6/r10.anchor: Buna göre âyette müşrikler, Hz. Peygamber’i kastederek telaffuz ettikleri “mecnun” kelimesini sözlük anlamında değil, onun cinlerle ilişkisinin bulunduğu anlamında kullanmış olabilirler (Ateş, V, 54)

BURHAN:v4p54/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p54/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p54/r5.claim: The unbelievers address the Prophet as one on whom the reminder descended and call him mad in the terms of their own belief.
BURHAN:v4p54/r5.anchor: يا أيها الذي نزل عليه الذكر إنك لمجنون
